clue.text: Mind being too hot?

parts.note: read as a brain that has overheated, a mind running a temperature, which is the name of an old-fashioned illness of delirium

explanation.surface: A question about whether one's mind is overheating.
explanation.definitionFit: The old term names a feverish inflammation of the head thought to cause delirium, literally a hot mind.

clue.text: He left here alone, without one, it's true

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word one is taken away from what remains
left means departed, so the word He goes out of the clue words that follow it

parts.note: the clue's words are the raw material for the two removals; the letters left do also run unbroken through them, a coincidence of the deletion
the clue's own word He names the letters to be removed
the clue's own word one names the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone departed and left another person all alone, and that is the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes HE out of HERE ALONE to give REALONE; 'without' then drops ONE, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine or actual is true rather than false.

clue.text: Sweethearts, according to one trashy novel

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: trashy suggests something cheap and messed up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheap romance novel tells us who the sweethearts are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashy' rearranges NOVEL to NLOVE, after I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweethearts are a couple who are romantically smitten with each other.

clue.text: Hemmed in by the water again, not knowing what to do

indicators.note: hemmed in by means surrounded by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a flood is a great mass of water
re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone cut off by floodwater once more is at a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a flood victim; 'the water' is the noun for the outer piece, and 'Hemmed in by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stumped or baffled leaves a person at a loss, the informal sense of knocked flat.

clue.text: The front clasps I find useless

indicators.note: clasps means holds tight, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the van is the front of an army, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A brooch's clasp at the front turns out to be of no use.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN as 'the front' comes from vanguard, the leading part of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort made in vain achieves nothing, so it is futile.

clue.text: Annoys, sending in day after day silly questions

indicators.note: sending in means putting inside, so the days go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to rile someone is to annoy them

indicators.note: after joins the two day letters one behind the other

parts.note: D again abbreviates day
D again abbreviates day

explanation.surface: Someone irritates others by asking foolish questions day after day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending in' places DD (day after day) inside RILES.
explanation.definitionFit: Conundrums are puzzling questions, often posed as jokes with a pun for an answer.

clue.text: A fondness for joining things

explanation.surface: A liking for connecting objects together.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotional bond is a fondness, and a device fixing one part to another is a connector.

clue.text: Slowly describing the little square

explanation.surface: A small square is described at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual progress goes little by little, and a square measuring one unit on each side is that size.

clue.text: Heads turn in shock

indicators.note: turn means the word for heads is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: People's heads turn in surprise at something shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to daze or stagger them.

clue.text: Make you think of the telephone warning

explanation.surface: A phone call that warns you about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to bring it back into memory; read literally, a phone ring telling you to watch out.

clue.text: Return to find caught in the hated trap and free

indicators.note: trap means hold, so the caught letter is held inside the other piece
return means the word hated is sent back and read in reverse

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone must go back to a dreaded trap to release what has been caught in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses HATED to DETAH; 'trap' signals the container round C. 'the' and 'to find' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate one thing from another is to free or unfasten it.

clue.text: Lingered anxiously near when he had to ring through

indicators.note: to ring means to encircle, so he surrounds the next word

parts.note: taken as written
over means through or finished, as in the game is over
'd is the shortened form of had

explanation.surface: Someone waited nervously close by while a man had to telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ring' makes he surround the word for through; 'when he had' reads like narrative but supplies two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay close by uncertainly is to hang about, like a bird holding position in the air.

clue.text: Are they inhabited by denizens of the deep?

definitions.text: Are they inhabited by denizens of the deep?

parts.words: Are they inhabited by denizens of the deep?
parts.note: sea creatures live in the seas, which for a nation are its own coastal seas, so the creatures' habitat is a fishy kind of residence

explanation.surface: A question about where sea creatures live.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's coastal seas are its own seas, and sea creatures live there.

clue.text: Bloodthirsty member of the team?

parts.note: a team member who wields a bat in cricket may be read as a creature that drinks blood

explanation.surface: A team player who is out for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical American flying mammal feeds on blood, and a bat is also what a cricketer or batter uses.

clue.text: Cuts on the gambling table!

explanation.surface: A gambler loses money at the tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook chops food into cubes; small cubes with spots are rolled when gambling.

clue.text: Such problems as dieticians have to discuss?

definitions.text: Such problems as dieticians have to discuss?

parts.words: Such problems as dieticians have to discuss?
parts.note: serious problems are described as heavy ones, and the people who help clients slim deal literally with heaviness

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of issues nutritionists talk about.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious matter is called heavy, and dieticians deal in pounds lost and gained.

clue.text: Accepts slang, though it's tiresome

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with slang even though it is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slang' marks the first sense as informal: 'I won't wear it' means I won't accept it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to tolerate an idea is to put up with it; something tiring and draining is wearing on you.

clue.text: Seedy haunts for such a rich man

explanation.surface: A wealthy man frequents shabby bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the traditional name for the rich man in Jesus's parable of the rich man and Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleazy bars are low drinking dens; the biblical rich man of the parable is traditionally named so.

clue.text: Tailless ape, female

indicators.note: tailless means without its tail, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to ape someone is to mimic them

explanation.surface: A female ape that has no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ape' is a verb here, not the animal: MIMIC loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's name, best known as the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème.

clue.text: Nut and vegetable

explanation.surface: Two kinds of food are offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses both words for the head; a broad or runner kind is a pod vegetable.

clue.text: Mentioned at least four trees

indicators.note: mentioned means said out loud, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: more than one couple means two twos, so at least four things

explanation.surface: Someone names at least four trees.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIRS, two or more couples, is at least four things; 'Mentioned' gives its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees of this kind bear the familiar pear-shaped fruit.

clue.text: Line calls

parts.note: read as an umpire's calls on a tennis line, but really the cues giving actors forgotten lines

explanation.surface: A tennis official's decisions about the line.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre a forgotten line is supplied by a whispered cue from the wings.

clue.text: Say happily it's raised support

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the whole run is written upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: a cat that purrs is saying it is happy
the clue's own letters, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully says that something has been held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PURR plus ITS upwards to STIRRUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The loop hanging from a saddle supports the rider's foot.

clue.text: They serve drinks when one is shown in

indicators.note: is shown in means ushered inside, so the one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: waters are drinks, as in mineral waters
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Drinks are served once a customer has been shown to a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is shown in' signals the container, reading in the surface like a customer being seated.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant staff who bring food and drink to tables are servers.

clue.text: Pull out in time

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' is a prison sentence, as in doing a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to pull it longer; a term in jail is slang for a period of time.

clue.text: Two people in the DIY shop

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
Mel is a man's or woman's name

explanation.surface: A couple are browsing in a hardware store.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names no people: the two are the names ENA and MEL. The definition is loose, a paint you would find on a do-it-yourself shop's shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy paint sold for woodwork and metal is stocked by home-improvement stores.

clue.text: Is among those people having a belief

indicators.note: among means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: It is among a group of people who share a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the container; 'having a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith in a god or gods is a religious conviction.

clue.text: Not so sound, having a hole when you open it

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters of so come out of sound

parts.note: the clue's own word so names the letters to be removed
O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: A doubtful item with a hole that appears once you open it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' removes S and O from the clue word sound, leaving UND; 'when you' is link material before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a knot or a button is to release or loosen it.

clue.text: Drop the title

explanation.surface: Someone loses their title.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to catch something is to let it fall; an unmarried woman's honorific is used before her name.

clue.text: The servant, given money, let the man try to break in

indicators.note: in means inside, so the scrambled letters go into the other word

parts.note: being paid means being given money

indicators.note: to break means to smash up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant who has been paid allowed a man to break into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' rearranges MAN TRY into ANTRYM; 'let the' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A household servant employed to look after the larder and food stores.

clue.text: Are educators and stern

explanation.surface: Teachers are strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents who bring up children act as their teachers; the back of a ship is its stern.

clue.text: Oxford would be dull without it

definitions.text: Oxford would be dull without it

parts.words: Oxford would be dull without it
parts.note: Oxford seems to be the university city, but an oxford is a lace-up leather shoe that needs shining

explanation.surface: Oxford would be a boring place without something.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxy cream rubbed onto leather footwear keeps it shiny.
